newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rice exports seen rising in December - trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian rice exports seen rising in December - trade.

text.p: Indian rice exports are expected to pick up during December once Vietnam's rice harvest is over, grain traders said on Thursday.
"Once Vietnam is out we can push our (rice) cargoes," Yogesh Dawda, an official at R.T. Exports, a Bombay-based foodgrains company, said.
"During December-January, Indian rice exports will pick-up as Vietnam's rice supplies will be over by that time," he said.
Traders said Indian non-Basmati rice is currently quoted around $15 a tonne above Vietnamese rice.
Indian five per cent broken non-Basmati rice was indicated quoted at $295 a tonne FOB Western ports, 10 percent grade at $280-285, 15 percent at $255-260 and 25 percent at $240 a tonne.
Traders said Indian rice exporters have signed contracts to export nearly one million tonnes of rice from the new crop for November and December shipment.
"Overseas deals of around one million tonnes of rice to be shipped during November-December has been signed," said an official in a New Delhi foodgrains export firm.
Traders said the Indian rice harvest is in full flow in most states.
"Around 15,000-20,000 tonnes of rice is arriving in the Indian markets every day," said Prem Garg, managing director of Sri Lal Mahal Overseas Ltd, a foodgrains exporter.
Gard said shipments of around 25,000 tonnes of five percent broken non-Basmati rice to Mauritius were currently taking place.
Traders said Jordan has expressed interest to buy around 25,000 tonnes of Indian rice.
"But probably the deals (with Jordan) will be government to government," said an exporter.
